overview.notice: Simulated paper-trading results. Figures based on fixture data are not validated performance. Confidence is a strength score, not a probability. Nothing here changes any setting.

avgWin.definition: mean net P&L of winning outcomes

avgLoss.definition: mean net P&L of losing outcomes (negative)

winRate.definition: wins / all eligible outcomes (net P&L > 0); breakeven counts as resolved and not a win; 95% Wilson interval

lossRate.definition: losses / all eligible outcomes (net P&L < 0); win rate + loss rate + breakeven share = 1; 95% Wilson interval

slippage.note: the reference price is not recorded for paper fills, so slippage cannot be measured; it is included in the fill prices but not separable

rMultiple.definition: net P&L / planned risk (initial stop distance x initial quantity); outcomes without a recorded R are excluded and counted here

costImpact.definition: costs as a percentage of the absolute gross P&L

expectancyR.definition: mean realised R-multiple (unrounded, 8-place fixed point); reported only with at least the minimum sample, with a 95% t interval
expectancyR.intervalMethod: 95% interval of the mean, Student's t with n-1 degrees of freedom

maxDrawdown.basis: largest fall of cumulative net P&L from its running peak, in closing order; the series starts at 0 and is not an account equity curve

payoffRatio.definition: average win / absolute average loss, computed in exact decimals (`exact` is the 8-place result, `value` its rounding to 4 places); null without both a win and a loss

profitFactor.definition: sum of winning net P&L / absolute sum of losing net P&L, in exact decimals (`exact` is the 8-place result); null without losses or below the minimum sample
profitFactor.intervalNote: no interval is reported: a ratio of sums has no exact small-sample interval and none is estimated or invented

maxDrawdownPct.reason: a percentage drawdown needs an account equity curve (capital over time), which is not recorded; the drawdown above is of cumulative net P&L only
maxDrawdownPct.definition: largest peak-to-trough fall of account equity as a percentage of the peak

data.statement: fixture-backed paper outcomes: 1 eligible outcome(s), fewer than the fewer than 30 eligible outcomes; no performance figure is reported (INSUFFICIENT_DATA).

avgWin.definition: mean net P&L of winning outcomes

avgLoss.definition: mean net P&L of losing outcomes (negative)

winRate.definition: wins / all eligible outcomes (net P&L > 0); breakeven counts as resolved and not a win; 95% Wilson interval

lossRate.definition: losses / all eligible outcomes (net P&L < 0); win rate + loss rate + breakeven share = 1; 95% Wilson interval

slippage.note: the reference price is not recorded for paper fills, so slippage cannot be measured; it is included in the fill prices but not separable

rMultiple.definition: net P&L / planned risk (initial stop distance x initial quantity); outcomes without a recorded R are excluded and counted here

costImpact.definition: costs as a percentage of the absolute gross P&L

expectancyR.definition: mean realised R-multiple (unrounded, 8-place fixed point); reported only with at least the minimum sample, with a 95% t interval
expectancyR.intervalMethod: 95% interval of the mean, Student's t with n-1 degrees of freedom

maxDrawdown.basis: largest fall of cumulative net P&L from its running peak, in closing order; the series starts at 0 and is not an account equity curve

payoffRatio.definition: average win / absolute average loss, computed in exact decimals (`exact` is the 8-place result, `value` its rounding to 4 places); null without both a win and a loss

profitFactor.definition: sum of winning net P&L / absolute sum of losing net P&L, in exact decimals (`exact` is the 8-place result); null without losses or below the minimum sample
profitFactor.intervalNote: no interval is reported: a ratio of sums has no exact small-sample interval and none is estimated or invented

maxDrawdownPct.reason: a percentage drawdown needs an account equity curve (capital over time), which is not recorded; the drawdown above is of cumulative net P&L only
maxDrawdownPct.definition: largest peak-to-trough fall of account equity as a percentage of the peak

expectancyMoney.definition: mean net P&L per eligible outcome

limitations: the drawdown is of cumulative net P&L, not an account equity curve
built on fixture-backed data: this describes the simulation, not the market
paper (simulated) results only; no live trading performance exists
association in a small history, not a forecast
